edges.description: A dense opacity in early infancy deprives the developing visual system of a formed image, causing deprivation amblyopia unless the lens is removed early.
Nystagmus follows early form deprivation from a dense congenital opacity and is more frequent when surgery is delayed.

edges.limitations: The mutant allele is an overexpressed transgene on a background with two normal mouse Crygc copies, so the dose of mutant protein differs from a heterozygous patient, and the stress response has not been examined in human lens tissue.

edges.limitations: The mouse allele is not a human variant, and the mouse gamma-crystallin cluster differs from the human one, so the contribution of the mutant protein to the lens protein pool may not match.

nodes.description: Deprivation amblyopia is the main threat to vision from a dense congenital opacity.

evidence.reference_title: Novel CRYGC Mutation in Conserved Ultraviolet-Protective Tryptophan (p.Trp131Arg) Is Linked to Autosomal Dominant Congenital Cataract.
evidence.snippet: Congenital cataract (CC), the most prevalent cause of childhood blindness and amblyopia, necessitates prompt and precise genetic diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: The gamma-crystallins and human cataracts: a puzzle made clearer.
evidence.snippet: To our knowledge, these findings are the first evidence of an involvement of CRYGC and support the role of CRYGD in human cataract formation.

evidence.reference_title: A 5-base insertion in the gammaC-crystallin gene is associated with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract.
evidence.snippet: The gammaD-crystallin gene shows no abnormalities, but a 5-bp duplication within exon 2 of the gammaC-crystallin gene has been found in one allele of each affected family member and is absent from both unaffected family members and unaffected controls.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations in CRYGC are associated with congenital cataracts in Chinese families.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in the CRYGC were responsible for 4.1% Chinese ADCC families in our cohort.

evidence.reference_title: Evaluating gene-disease relationship strength in crystallin genes in association with pediatric cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Seven genes (CRYAA, CRYAB, CRYBA1, CRYBB1, CRYBB2, CRYGC, CRYGD) scored as Definitively associated with autosomal dominant (AD) inherited pediatric cataracts.

nodes.description: Transgenic mice expressing the human 5-bp duplication allele develop cataracts of variable onset and severity; severe lenses have higher transgene expression and activate the unfolded protein response.

Heterozygous missense, nonsense and frameshift variants in CRYGC. Missense alleles change conserved residues in either domain (T5P, R48H, G129C, W131R, S166F, R168W). Nonsense and frameshift alleles (the c.119_123dup 5-bp duplication, C109X, E128*, Y139X, W157X and others) truncate the protein and remove one or both C-terminal Greek key motifs.

evidence.reference_title: The gamma-crystallins and human cataracts: a puzzle made clearer.
evidence.snippet: Further analysis of the original Coppock-like-cataract family identified a missense mutation in a highly conserved segment of exon 2 of CRYGC.

evidence.reference_title: A 5-base insertion in the gammaC-crystallin gene is associated with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract.
evidence.snippet: This mutation disrupts the reading frame of the gammaC-crystallin coding sequence and is predicted to result in the synthesis of an unstable gammaC-crystallin with 38 amino acids of the first "Greek key" motif followed by 52 random amino acids.

evidence.reference_title: A nonsense mutation in CRYGC associated with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: One and a half Greek key motifs at the COOH-terminus were found to be absent in the structural model of the mutant truncated gammaC-crystallin.

nodes.description: Lens extraction is the standard management of visually significant CRYGC cataract, from infancy for dense congenital opacities. For dense bilateral congenital cataract, the timing of surgery in the first weeks of life governs visual outcome; this evidence comes from cohorts that were not genotyped. No CRYGC-specific therapy exists.

evidence.reference_title: A nonsense mutation of CRYGC associated with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataracts and microcornea in a Chinese pedigree.
evidence.snippet: Individual III:3 had cataract extraction performed at 6 years of age.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Landscape of Congenital Cataracts in a Swiss Cohort: Addressing Diagnostic Oversights in Nance-Horan Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: had nuclear cataracts and underwent surgery at 1 month

evidence.reference_title: The critical period for surgical treatment of dense congenital bilateral cataracts.
evidence.snippet: During weeks 0-14, mean visual acuity decreased by 1 line with each 3 weeks' delay in surgery.

nodes.description: Chlorambucil-induced dominant mutant with bilateral nuclear and radial lens opacity, small lenses and degeneration of fiber cells in the lens core.
Cataract is usually present at birth and bilateral; a de novo W131R patient was born with total bilateral cataract.

evidence.reference_title: Novel CRYGC Mutation in Conserved Ultraviolet-Protective Tryptophan (p.Trp131Arg) Is Linked to Autosomal Dominant Congenital Cataract.
evidence.snippet: Whole exome sequencing (WES) and copy number variation (CNV) analysis were conducted for variant identification in a patient born with a total binocular CC without a family history of CC.

evidence.reference_title: A family with autosomal dominant primary congenital cataract associated with a CRYGC mutation: evidence of clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: In the present study, we described a family with nuclear congenital cataract that segregated the CRYGC missense mutation c.502C>T.

nodes.description: Nuclear cataract; disrupts the C-terminal domain and lowers stability.

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation impairing the tertiary structure and stability of γC-crystallin (CRYGC) leads to cataract formation in humans and zebrafish lens.
evidence.snippet: we identified a novel, heterozygous c.385G<T mutation in CRYGC that resulted in the substitution of a highly conserved glycine by cysteine at codon 129 (p.Gly129Cys) in a three-generation Chinese family with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract by sequencing candidate genes.

nodes.description: Mutant gamma-C crystallin forms intracellular aggregates in cultured cells, including human lens epithelial cells. Mutant T5P also interacts less with itself and with other crystallins, and co-expressed alpha-A crystallin reduces its aggregation, which suggests that alpha-crystallin chaperone capacity limits aggregation in the lens.
nodes.id: Gamma-C Crystallin Aggregation in Lens Cells

evidence.reference_title: Protein-protein interactions involving congenital cataract T5P gammaC-crystallin mutant: a confocal fluorescence microscopy study.
evidence.snippet: The confocal fluorescence images show that cells expressing T5P gammaC-crystallin contain many protein aggregates, but cells co-expressing with either gammaC- or alphaA-crystallin reduce the aggregation considerably.

evidence.reference_title: Visualization of in situ intracellular aggregation of two cataract-associated human gamma-crystallin mutants: lose a tail, lose transparency.
evidence.snippet: Transfection of the EGFP-tagged mutant cDNAs into several cell lines led to the visualization of aggregates, whereas that of wild-type cDNAs did not.

evidence.reference_title: Alteration of protein-protein interactions of congenital cataract crystallin mutants.
evidence.snippet: For the T5P gammaC-crystallin, most of the interactions were decreased

nodes.description: Most tested alleles change the conformation of gamma-C crystallin and lower its stability. T5P alters conformation and stability and is largely insoluble when overexpressed; G129C disrupts the C-terminal domain and sharply lowers thermal stability; the 5-bp duplication loses secondary and tertiary structure; and the W157X truncation exposes hydrophobic side chains and lowers solubility.

evidence.reference_title: Conformational change and destabilization of cataract gammaC-crystallin T5P mutant.
evidence.snippet: During cloning and overexpression, the majority of T5P mutant was found in the inclusion body.

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation impairing the tertiary structure and stability of γC-crystallin (CRYGC) leads to cataract formation in humans and zebrafish lens.
evidence.snippet: The mutation led to a dramatic decrease in the thermal stability of γC-crystallin

evidence.reference_title: Mutation causing self-aggregation in human gammaC-crystallin leading to congenital cataract.
evidence.snippet: The authors found that the 5-bp insertion led to a loss of secondary and tertiary structures of the molecule and to an enhanced tendency of self-aggregation into light-scattering particles, offering a possible factor in lens opacification.

evidence.reference_title: Visualization of in situ intracellular aggregation of two cataract-associated human gamma-crystallin mutants: lose a tail, lose transparency.
evidence.snippet: The deletion of C-terminal 18 residues of human gammaC- and gammaD-crystallins exposes the side chains of several hydrophobic residues in the sequence to the solvent, causing the molecule to self-aggregate.

nodes.description: R168W was first reported with lamellar cataract; a later family with the same allele had nuclear cataract.

evidence.reference_title: A family with autosomal dominant primary congenital cataract associated with a CRYGC mutation: evidence of clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: This mutation has been associated with the phenotype of lamellar cataract but is also considered a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the NCBI database.

nodes.description: In transgenic mice carrying the human 5-bp duplication allele, lenses with severe cataract show PERK-dependent unfolded protein response activation with induction of autophagy and apoptosis, and severity tracks transgene expression level. This has been shown only for the 5-bp duplication and only in mice.
nodes.id: Lens Fiber Cell Unfolded Protein Response and Apoptosis

animal_models.genotype: Transgenic human CRYGC c.119_123dup (p.Cys42AlafsX63) minigene driven by the chicken betaB1-crystallin promoter
animal_models.name: CRYGC 5-bp duplication transgenic mouse

evidence.reference_title: The c.119-123dup5bp mutation in human γC-crystallin destabilizes the protein and activates the unfolded protein response to cause highly variable cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Thus, high levels of CRYGC5bpdup transgene expression in severely affected lenses induces UPRer and UPRmt stress responses primarily through the PERK-dependent and Atf4/Atf5/Ddit3 pathways respectively, inducing autophagy and apoptosis and thence congenital nuclear cataracts.

nodes.description: Aggregated protein and damaged fiber cells scatter light, producing lens opacities that are most often nuclear, and sometimes dust-like (Coppock-like), zonular pulverulent or lamellar. Severity varies between relatives carrying the same allele.
nodes.id: Lens Light Scattering and Loss of Transparency

animal_models.genotype: Crygc(Chl3), 6-bp in-frame deletion in exon 3 removing Gly and Arg in the fourth Greek key motif; dominant
animal_models.name: Crygc Chl3 mouse

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation impairing the tertiary structure and stability of γC-crystallin (CRYGC) leads to cataract formation in humans and zebrafish lens.
evidence.snippet: Using zebrafish as a model, we demonstrated that γC-crystallin p.Gly129Cys mutant caused the vacuole and the incomplete denucleation of lens, recapitulating the cataract phenotype in human beings.

evidence.reference_title: A novel CRYGC E128* mutation underlying an autosomal dominant nuclear cataract in a south Indian kindred.
evidence.snippet: Molecular function analysis of this novel mutation (p. E128*, CRYGC) in the zebrafish indicated this mutation to impair lens transparency.

nodes.description: Nuclear cataract is the most frequently reported morphology, including in most truncating-allele families. The Coppock-like T5P cataract is a dust-like opacity of the fetal nucleus.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations in CRYGC are associated with congenital cataracts in Chinese families.
evidence.snippet: Six novel CRYGC mutations (p.Asp65ThrfsX38, p.Arg142GlyfsX5, p.Arg142AlafsX22, p.Tyr144X, p.Arg169X, and p.Tyr46Asp) were identified in other six families with congenital nuclear cataracts, respectively.

evidence.reference_title: A nonsense mutation in CRYGC associated with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: A novel nonsense mutation in CRYGC was detected in a Chinese family with consistent autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract, providing clear evidence of a relationship between the genotype and the corresponding cataract phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Conformational change and destabilization of cataract gammaC-crystallin T5P mutant.
evidence.snippet: This mutation is associated with Coppock-like cataract, and has the phenotype of a dust-like opacity of the fetal lens nucleus.

nodes.description: Nystagmus is seen in patients whose dense congenital cataract was not removed early.

evidence.reference_title: A nonsense mutation in CRYGC associated with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: Obvious nystagmus was observed in all the patients except the 10-month-old proband who received phacoemulsification surgery in both eyes on presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Case Report: A de novo Variant of CRYGC Gene Associated With Congenital Cataract and Microphthalmia.
evidence.snippet: A congenital cataract patient with microphthalmia and nystagmus was recruited for this study.

nodes.description: Zonular pulverulent (powdery) opacities, highly variable between relatives, in the seven-generation 5-bp duplication family; pulverulent cataract was also reported with R48H.

evidence.reference_title: A 5-base insertion in the gammaC-crystallin gene is associated with autosomal dominant variable zonular pulverulent cataract.
evidence.snippet: A seven-generation family with 30 members affected by highly variable autosomal dominant zonular pulverulent cataracts has been previously described.

evidence.reference_title: A CRYGC gene mutation associated with autosomal dominant pulverulent cataract.
evidence.snippet: In the present study, we described a family with pulverulent congenital cataract that segregated the c.143G>A mutation (p.R48H) in the CRYGC gene.

nodes.description: Lamellar or nuclear cataract; native-like fold with increased self-aggregation.

evidence.reference_title: A family with autosomal dominant primary congenital cataract associated with a CRYGC mutation: evidence of clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: Our data and previous report support that R168W is the actual disease-causing mutation and should no longer be considered a SNP.

nodes.description: The R168W protein has a near-normal conformation and stability but a greater tendency to self-aggregate and scatter light, showing that unfolding is not required for CRYGC cataract.
nodes.id: Self-Aggregation of Conformationally Normal Gamma-C Crystallin

evidence.reference_title: Mutation causing self-aggregation in human gammaC-crystallin leading to congenital cataract.
evidence.snippet: These results support the idea that unfolding or structural destabilization is not always necessary for crystallin-associated cataractogenesis.

nodes.description: Coppock-like cataract allele; misfolded, destabilized and largely insoluble.

evidence.reference_title: Conformational change and destabilization of cataract gammaC-crystallin T5P mutant.
evidence.snippet: The T5P mutation obviously changes conformation and decreases conformational stability.

nodes.description: Reduced vision from the lens opacity and its developmental complications.

evidence.reference_title: A nonsense mutation in CRYGC associated with autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: Hereditary congenital cataract (OMIM 604307) is an opacification of the eye lens that frequently results in visual impairment or even blindness during infancy or early childhood.

nodes.description: Truncates the C-terminal 18 residues; nuclear cataract with microcornea; also reported de novo.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Landscape of Congenital Cataracts in a Swiss Cohort: Addressing Diagnostic Oversights in Nance-Horan Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: He is the only carrier of the variant thus it being de novo.

nodes.description: Five-base duplication in exon 2 causing a frameshift; variable zonular pulverulent cataract in a seven-generation family.

evidence.reference_title: The c.119-123dup5bp mutation in human γC-crystallin destabilizes the protein and activates the unfolded protein response to cause highly variable cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Here we investigate the molecular mechanism of cataractogenesis of the CRYGC c.119-123dupGCGGC (p.Cys42AlafsX63) (CRYGC5bpdup) mutation.
